entities.name: Pan Chakri, Chao Phraya Kosathibodi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Chao Phraya Kosathibodi, born Pan, commonly known as Kosa Pan, was a prominent Siamese nobleman during the reign of King Narai of the Ayutthaya Kingdom. He is best remembered for leading the second Siamese embassy to France in 1686. He was preceded to France by the first Siamese embassy to France, which had been composed of two Siamese ambassadors and Father Bénigne Vachet, who had left Siam for France on January 5, 1684.

Chao Phraya Kosathibodi's significance lies in his role as a key figure in the diplomatic relations between Siam and France during the 17th century. His embassy to France marked a significant turning point in the establishment of trade and cultural exchanges between the two nations.

The Ayutthaya Kingdom's continued influence during the 17th century was a result of Chao Phraya Kosathibodi's efforts to strengthen relations with European powers. His legacy can be seen in the lasting impact of Siamese diplomacy on the region's history.

As a prominent figure in the kingdom, Chao Phraya Kosathibodi's life and achievements serve as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Ayutthaya Kingdom.

In the words of Father Bénigne Vachet, 'He was a great and generous prince, who had a particular fondness for our Lord Jesus Christ.'
